text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 0

Both you and the appointed candidate are women, so sex was almost certainly not a factor in the hiring decision. Raising the panel’s gender composition would appear unfounded, detract from your professional standing, and damage relationships within the academic community.

Hiring committees frequently weigh criteria beyond publication counts. The department likely valued the candidate’s industry experience to support applied courses, industry partnerships, or specific curricular needs, alongside her interview performance. 

When you follow up regarding feedback, keep the inquiry strictly professional. Ask constructive questions about how to strengthen your application and departmental fit for future academic roles rather than focusing on panel demographics.
